name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with PVI of D+18
Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~94%
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but no strong GOP recruit
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean and a favorable national environment make this a Safe Democratic hold even without Crockett on the ballot. Allred's name recognition and dominant fundraising against an underfunded Republican reinforce the fundamentals, and markets agree.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually weak Democratic turnout operation in a low-profile open seat could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Dallas-area seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Texas, with a partisan lean of D+18. Jasmine Crockett is retiring to run for Senate, but the Democratic bench here is deep, and former Rep. Colin Allred enters as a well-known candidate who has raised more than $7.4 million for the race. Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported minimal fundraising and little outside support.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 94%. The seat remains Safe Democratic, with modest uncertainty from the open-seat transition.
